title: Adobe ends an 18-year era as AI pressure mounts
content:
Adobe is handing over control to a new CEO after the current CEO spent 18 years in the role, as artificial intelligence is set to disrupt the software company that powers Photoshop and Creative Cloud.
Adobe (ADBE) is undergoing one of its largest leadership overhauls ever at a particularly challenging time for investors.
Anil Chakravarthy will become president and CEO of software giant Adobe, succeeding Shantanu Narayen, who has been at the helm for more than 18 years. Chakravarthy will take over on Dec. 1, and Narayen will move to the role of executive chair.
But Wall Street's response hinted at the scale of the task confronting Adobe's new boss.
Adobe shares fell nearly 7% on Sept. 4, after the leadership announcement and David Wadhwani's departure. Wadhwani ran Adobe's creativity and productivity business and was a potential CEO candidate.
After falling more than 21% in 2025, the stock had fallen 18% in 2026 before Friday Sept 4.
But the greater issue is that generative AI is coming for the industry that Adobe has controlled for decades, and investors are waiting for proof that Adobe can transform its own AI technologies into enough growth to secure its business.
Adobe's leadership shakeup comes at a critical moment
Chakravarthy joined Adobe in 2020 after serving as CEO of Informatica. He oversaw Adobe's Digital Experience business first, then ran international field operations and finally led its Customer Experience Orchestration business.
That background might be a key hint as to where Adobe is headed.
Adobe says it's using agentic AI more in its corporate solutions to tailor interactions enterprises have with their consumers.
But the succession also heralds another big shift.
Wadhwani, who has overseen Adobe's creative and productivity division for almost five years, said he was stepping down after Chakravarthy's appointment. Wadhwani was said to be a possible contender for the CEO role.
So Adobe is not just replacing the CEO. The corporation is also facing what may be the largest technical challenge to its creative-software brand since cloud computing emerged.
Now investors have to decide whether Chakravarthy can take that disruption and reshape it once again.
Wall Street sees a major AI threat to Adobe
Adobe's main challenge is that it lacks artificial intelligence.
The business has been working hard to grow Firefly and add generative AI capabilities to products like Photoshop and its larger creative suite.
The question is whether AI is changing the economics of creative software quicker than Adobe can commercialize those goods.
Morgan Stanley downgraded Adobe to Underweight from Equalweight in July and slashed its price target to $240 from $365. The firm cited several simultaneous transitions, including Adobe's freemium strategy, leadership changes, and increased AI investment.
More fundamentally, Morgan Stanley questioned the vulnerability of Creative Cloud's recurring income to being replaced by generative AI.
This is the heart of Adobe's problem.
AI technologies are democratizing the ability to create complex images and video that previously required specific technical skills, which took time and practice to master. Adobe is also competing with firms like Canva and Figma, and newer generative AI platforms are transforming the way people create digital material.
Barclays recently raised its Adobe price target to $295 from $250 while maintaining an Equalweight rating, while RBC Capital increased its target to $315 from $285 and maintained an Outperform rating.
The fight reveals exactly how challenging it has become for Wall Street to value Adobe.
Adobe's new CEO inherits an AI problem worth billions
The shift in leadership at Adobe comes only days before another big test.
Adobe's fiscal third-quarter earnings release is due Sept. 10, providing investors their first big chance since the CEO announcement to gauge Adobe's financial performance and its AI strategy. The leadership announcement itself came as Adobe confirmed the date for results.
Adobe isn't going into that report empty-handed.
Reuters reported that the business upgraded its annual profit prediction in June due to rising demand for its AI-powered goods.
But investors want more than that.
They want proof that standard artificial intelligence can protect—and ultimately accelerate, the steady income stream Adobe has created with products such as Photoshop, Illustrator, and Creative Cloud.
The nomination of Chakravarthy is significant beyond an executive shift.
Narayen helped turn Adobe from a packaged software company into a cloud subscription juggernaut. So now Chakravarthy inherits a new transformation: the challenge of showing Adobe can still be vital when generative AI makes it much simpler to create professional-looking content.
The decline in the stock implies investors aren't convinced yet.
And after two years of significant share-price loss, Adobe's new CEO doesn't have the luxury of looking at AI as just another product cycle.
He's taking over a debate over whether one of software's best brands can stay just as valuable in an AI-first society.

report.summary: Adobe appoints Anil Chakravarthy CEO as Shantanu Narayen steps down after 18 years, with generative AI disrupting its creative software market.
report.background: Shantanu Narayen reshaped Adobe from a packaged, boxed-software maker into a cloud subscription powerhouse, with Photoshop and Creative Cloud generating steady recurring revenue. That model now faces a historic challenge from generative AI, which lets non-professionals create sophisticated images and video without learning complex tools. Investors fear these tools could erode Adobe's subscription base and pricing power, as competitors like Canva, Figma, and newer generative platforms offer simpler and sometimes cheaper workflows. Adobe's stock has fallen steeply, and analysts are split on whether the company's Firefly AI and agentic enterprise features can close the gap. The leadership transition is therefore not just a succession event but an admission that Adobe must adapt again. Chakravarthy's experience in enterprise and customer experience suggests the next growth wave is expected in AI-infused business software, not just creative apps.
key_points: Shantanu Narayen is stepping down after more than 18 years as Adobe CEO, becoming executive chairman. Anil Chakravarthy, who joined Adobe in 2020 from Informatica and led digital experience and customer experience operations, will take over on Dec. 1. David Wadhwani, head of creative products and a possible contender, is leaving.

Adobe shares fell almost 7% after the leadership announcement and are down sharply over 2025 and 2026. Morgan Stanley downgraded Adobe in July, cutting its price target to $240 from $365 and flagging risks from creative-software economics, freemium strategy, and leadership changes.

Generative AI is the core threat: tools that create professional images and video without specialized skills undermine Photoshop and Creative Cloud subscriptions. Adobe competes with Canva, Figma, and new AI platforms, leaving investors uncertain whether Firefly features can generate enough growth to protect recurring revenue.

Chakravarthy's background lies in enterprise software and customer experience orchestration, and Adobe says it is pushing agentic AI in corporate tools. That suggests the new CEO may focus more on business-facing AI services than on defending the creative desktop, marking a strategic shift.

Adobe's fiscal third-quarter earnings on Sept. 10 will be an early test for the new strategy. Adobe raised its annual profit forecast in June on demand for AI products, but after two years of pressure the market needs proof that AI can monetize without cannibalizing high-margin subscriptions.
report.impact: For the AI industry, Adobe's leadership shakeup signals that incumbents can no longer assume product distribution protects the economics of creativity. For developers, it may accelerate openings in Adobe platforms, plus more AI APIs for image and video generation agents. Regular users may see more generative features integrated into Photoshop, but also more attempts to tie AI into subscriptions. The deeper issue is that if Adobe fails to monetize AI, this will legitimize a shift toward AI-native creation tools, showing that generative AI disrupts not only content creation but the business models built around professional skills. Incoming CEO Chakravarthy must balance protecting Creative Cloud revenue with embracing AI that could make subscriptions less necessary; anything less may keep the stock under pressure.
report.tools: For readers exploring the AI disruption Adobe faces, tools to watch include Adobe Firefly and Adobe Experience Platform agentic AI APIs. To compare alternatives, try open-source Stable Diffusion via ComfyUI or InvokeAI for image generation, GIMP with AI plugins for editing, and Penpot as an open-source collaborative design option. These show what replacement workflows look like and help evaluate whether Adobe's subscription-based AI will retain value.
